easy.def: A holy book that many people read in church.
examples: The family has a Bible.
She reads the Bible.
There are stories in the Bible.

more.def: The holy book of the Christian religion, and the first part is also holy to Jews.
examples: The family read from the Bible.
Many stories in the Bible are very old.
The Bible has been translated into many languages.

easy.def: A two-wheeled vehicle you ride by pedaling.
examples: I ride my bicycle.
The bicycle has a bell.
She got a new bicycle.

more.def: A vehicle with two wheels that you ride by pushing pedals with your feet.
examples: I ride my bicycle to school.
The bicycle has a bell and a basket.
She got a new bicycle for her birthday.

easy.def: An offer of a price.
examples: He made a bid for the painting.
My bid was ten dollars.
The highest bid wins.

more.def: An offer to pay a certain amount of money for something.
examples: He made a bid of ten dollars for the painting.
The highest bid won the old clock.
Her bid was too low.

easy.def: To offer a price for something.
examples: I bid ten dollars.
She bid on the lamp.
He bid for the toy.

more.def: To offer an amount of money for something, as at an auction.
examples: I bid ten dollars for the chair.
She bid on the old lamp.
They bid against each other for the painting.

easy.def: Offering how much money you will pay at a sale.
examples: The bidding started at five dollars.
The bidding was fast.
Bidding went up quickly.

more.def: The act of offering a price for something at an auction.
examples: The bidding for the painting began at ten dollars.
Bidding at the school auction was quick and exciting.
The bidding stopped when no one offered a higher price.

easy.def: What someone tells you to do.
examples: The dog did my bidding.
He did his mom's bidding.
The servant did the king's bidding.

more.def: A command or request that you are expected to follow.
examples: In the story, the genie does whatever his master asks and does his bidding.
The knights did the king's bidding.
She did her teacher's bidding and handed out the papers.

easy.def: Large in size.
examples: An elephant is big.
I have a big dog.
It is a big house.

more.def: Large in size, amount, or importance.
examples: A big wave crashed onto the sandy beach.
The school is having a big party for the end of the year.
Winning the contest was a big moment for her.

easy.def: A two-wheeled machine you pedal.
examples: I ride my bike.
My bike is red.
She rode her bike to school.

more.def: A vehicle with two wheels that you move by pushing pedals.
examples: I ride my bike to school.
She pumped air into her bike tires.
We went for a long bike ride.

easy.def: A person who rides a bike.
examples: The biker rode up the hill.
A biker passed us.
The biker wore a helmet.

more.def: A person who rides a bicycle or a motorcycle.
examples: The biker wore a helmet and rode carefully down the path.
A group of bikers rode through the park on Saturday.
The biker stopped at the red light.

easy.def: A swimsuit that comes in two small pieces.
examples: She wore a bikini at the beach.
The bikini is yellow.
A bikini dries fast.

more.def: A two-piece swimsuit worn at the beach or pool.
examples: She packed a bikini and a towel for the beach trip.
The pool store sold a red bikini and a blue one.
A bikini was drying on the line next to the towels.

easy.def: A very big number, one thousand millions.
examples: There are billions of stars.
A billion is huge.
The country has a billion people.

more.def: The number 1,000,000,000, which is one thousand millions.
examples: There are billions of stars in the galaxy.
A billion is a thousand millions.
The earth has about eight billion people.

easy.def: A large container for storing things.
examples: Put the trash in the bin.
The toy bin is full.
The bin is blue.

more.def: A large box or container that is used for storing or collecting things.
examples: Put the recycling in the blue bin.
The toy bin in my room is full.
The grain was stored in a bin.

easy.def: To tie something together.
examples: I bind the sticks together.
She bound her hair.
We bound the books.

more.def: To tie or fasten things together tightly.
examples: I bound the sticks together with a string.
She bound her hair with a ribbon.
Dad bound the books with a rubber band.

easy.def: Having to do with living things.
examples: Eating is a biological need.
Plants are biological things.
Growing is a biological process.

more.def: Having to do with living things and the study of life.
examples: The biological parts of a cell work together.
Breathing is a biological function of every animal.
The scientists studied the biological processes of plants.

easy.def: The study of living things.
examples: I like biology.
Biology is science.
We study biology.

more.def: The science that studies plants, animals and all living things.
examples: I like biology class.
Biology teaches how animals live.
We studied plants in biology.

easy.def: An animal with feathers and wings.
examples: A bird sings.
The bird built a nest.
Birds eat seeds.

more.def: An animal with feathers, wings and a beak, that usually can fly.
examples: A bird built a nest in the tree.
Penguins are birds that cannot fly.
Owls are birds that hunt at night.

easy.def: A little bird.
examples: Look at the birdie.
The birdie sang.
A birdie sat on the fence.

more.def: A child's word for a small bird.
examples: Look at the pretty birdie!
The birdie sang in the tree.
A little birdie sat on the fence.

easy.def: The sweet sound that birds make.
examples: I love birdsong in the morning.
We heard birdsong.
Birdsong filled the woods.

more.def: The musical sounds that birds make, especially in the early morning.
examples: We woke up to the sound of birdsong outside the window.
Birdsong filled the woods in the early spring.
She recorded the birdsong with her tablet.

easy.def: When a baby comes into the world.
examples: We saw a picture from his birth.
The birth of a lamb is exciting.
Her birth was in the spring.

more.def: The time when a baby or animal is born.
examples: The farm was busy on the night of the foal's birth.
The nurse wrote the baby's weight at birth.
A birth certificate shows the date and place you were born.

easy.def: The day you were born, every year.
examples: Today is my birthday.
We have cake on my birthday.
Her birthday is in May.

more.def: The day each year that is the same date as the day you were born.
examples: My birthday is in the spring.
We sang to Grandpa on his birthday.
She turned eight on her birthday.

easy.def: A small, soft bread.
examples: I ate a biscuit.
The biscuit is warm.
She baked biscuits.

more.def: A small, soft, round bread that is baked quickly.
examples: I ate a warm biscuit with butter.
Grandma baked biscuits for breakfast.
He split the biscuit and added jam.

easy.def: A leader in some churches.
examples: The bishop gave a talk.
The bishop wore a tall hat.
The bishop visited.

more.def: A senior leader in some churches.
examples: The bishop visited our church on Sunday.
A bishop wears a tall hat.
The bishop gave a blessing.

easy.def: A piece in the game of chess.
examples: I moved my bishop.
The bishop is next to the king.
Bishops move on a slant.

more.def: A piece in chess that can move any distance on a slant.
examples: I moved my bishop across the board.
The bishop captured the knight.
A bishop stays on the same color of squares.

easy.def: A small piece or amount.
examples: I ate a bit of cake.
Add a bit of salt.
A bit of paper.

more.def: A small piece or a small amount of something.
examples: I found a bit of string on the floor.
Add a bit more water to the soup.
She was a bit shy on her first day.

easy.def: To use your teeth to cut or hold.
examples: I bite the apple.
The dog bit the toy.
Do not bite your pencil.

more.def: To use your teeth to cut, hold or crush something.
examples: Bite the apple and chew it well.
The puppy bit the rope toy.
Mosquitoes bite at night.

easy.def: A mouthful of food.
examples: Take a bite.
One bite of cake.
I took a bite of the apple.

more.def: A small amount of food taken into the mouth at one time.
examples: She took a big bite of the sandwich.
Have a bite of my pie.
He saved one bite for later.

easy.def: A small hurt from a bug or animal.
examples: I have a mosquito bite.
The bite is small.
A bee bite itches.

more.def: A small cut or sting made by an insect or animal.
examples: The mosquito bite on my arm itched.
The dog's bite did not break the skin.
He put cream on the bite.

easy.def: Having a sharp, unpleasant taste.
examples: The medicine tastes bitter.
The coffee was bitter.
The seeds are bitter.

more.def: Having a strong, sharp taste that is not sweet.
examples: The medicine tasted bitter.
Lemon peel can taste bitter.
The coffee was too bitter for me.

easy.def: Very cold.
examples: The wind is bitter.
It was a bitter day.
We felt the bitter cold.

more.def: Extremely cold and sharp.
examples: A bitter wind blew across the lake.
It was a bitter winter night.
We wore thick coats against the bitter cold.

easy.def: Very strange.
examples: The dream was bizarre.
A bizarre noise came.
He wore a bizarre hat.

more.def: Very odd and unusual.
examples: I had a bizarre dream about a flying cat.
A bizarre noise came from the attic.
He wore a bizarre hat with feathers.
